items.desc: Inspect Chrome, Firefox, and Safari tabs together

outro_card.title: TabWrangler
outro_card.subtitle: Terminal Tab Management
bullets: Unified tab visibility across Chrome, Firefox, and Safari
Fast keyboard filtering, sorting, and navigation
Hibernate idle tabs to save RAM, with full undo support

scenes.narration: TabWrangler aggregates open tabs across Chrome, Firefox, and Safari into a single terminal interface. Here is a walkthrough of its core features.

steps.say: The main table shows open tabs across all browsers with domain, title, memory, and status.
Pressing one narrows the scope to Google Chrome.
Pressing three switches to Safari tabs.
Pressing zero returns to the combined view.
Pressing slash activates live search across titles, URLs, and domains.
Typing doc filters the table down to matching documentation tabs.
Pressing escape clears the search query.
Pressing s toggles the sort order.
Pressing question mark opens the help modal with keyboard shortcuts and core concepts.
Pressing escape dismisses the help modal.
Pressing h hibernates the tab to free memory while keeping it open.
Pressing u wakes the hibernated tab back into memory.
Pressing c closes the selected tab and removes it.
Pressing u restores the closed tab.
Pressing q quits TabWrangler and exits to the terminal.

scenes.narration: TabWrangler provides tab visibility and resource control directly in the terminal. The project repository is shown on screen.
